title: Following a Trait to Its Gene

scenes.tts: Which stretch of which chromosome travels with a trait in a family, and which gene inside it is broken? Before DNA markers, a human disease gene could usually be located only if its protein, or a nearby known gene, was already guessed. A gene known only from its effect had no handle.
scenes.visual: Pedigree with affected members beside a chromosome bar marked with question marks; a gene known only from its effect.
scenes.narration: Which stretch of which chromosome travels with a trait in a family, and which gene inside it is broken? Before DNA markers, a human disease gene could usually be located only if its protein, or a nearby known gene, was already guessed. A gene known only from its effect had no handle.

scenes.tts: Collect families in which the trait segregates, with affected and unaffected members. Then read their DNA at variable markers spread across the genome. Each marker is typed in every family member, and tested for co-inheritance with the disease.
scenes.visual: Pedigree plus chromosome bar with markers; each person gets a genotype under the symbol.
scenes.narration: Collect families in which the trait segregates, with affected and unaffected members. Then read their DNA at variable markers spread across the genome. Each marker is typed in every family member, and tested for co-inheritance with the disease.

scenes.tts: The physical fact used is meiotic recombination. Markers close to the gene are rarely separated from it, so they travel with the trait. One percent recombination is called one centimorgan. A marker that follows the disease through the family, with few or no recombinants, is the signal of linkage.
scenes.visual: One allele follows the filled symbols through three generations; chromosomes cross over, a near marker stays with the gene.
scenes.narration: The physical fact used is meiotic recombination. Markers close to the gene are rarely separated from it, so they travel with the trait. One percent recombination is called one centimorgan. A marker that follows the disease through the family, with few or no recombinants, is the signal of linkage.

scenes.tts: Examine more recombinant chromosomes, from more meioses, and the linked interval shrinks. Then find the genes in the interval, using techniques that identify expressed genes there, and search them for mutations. Proof is the same gene carrying mutations in affected people, ideally different ones in unrelated families, and the mutant protein tested.
scenes.visual: Recombinant chromosome bars stack up, the shared band narrows; genes appear in it; one gene shows a mutation in affected people.
scenes.narration: Examine more recombinant chromosomes, from more meioses, and the linked interval shrinks. scenes.tts: The LOD score is the base ten log of a likelihood ratio: the probability of the data if the markers are linked, over the probability if they are unlinked. Idealised example: ten fully informative meioses, phase known, none recombinant, give a LOD of three point oh one. Traditionally, above three is called significant. One recombinant in ten drops it to one point six.
scenes.visual: Ten meiosis boxes fill one by one while a LOD bar rises to 3.01 past the threshold line; then one recombinant drops the bar to 1.60. Labelled idealised.
scenes.caption: The LOD score is the base ten log of a likelihood ratio: the probability of the data if the markers are linked, over the probability if they are unlinked. Idealised example: ten fully informative meioses, phase known, none recombinant, give a LOD of 3.01. Traditionally, above 3 is called significant. One recombinant in ten drops it to 1.6.
scenes.narration: The LOD score is the base ten log of a likelihood ratio: the probability of the data if the markers are linked, over the probability if they are unlinked. scenes.tts: A LOD of three is not proof. Since most loci are unlinked, it means odds of only about twenty to one for linkage, and will prove spurious in about one instance in twenty, so replicate in independent families. And a linked interval holds many genes: the loop-tail interval of the mouse held at least seventeen transcription units. So find a mutation in the gene itself.
scenes.visual: Odds bar 20:1 with one spurious in 20 and a replicate family check; an interval crowded with seventeen gene boxes, one tested for a mutation.

scenes.tts: In 1983, Gusella and colleagues linked the Huntington disease gene to a marker on chromosome four. In 1993 the collaborative group found an unstable, expanded C A G repeat in a new gene there, in all seventy-five families tested. A decade separated map from gene. In 1998, Beutler's group used two thousand and ninety-three meioses to confine the mouse mutation behind L P S resistance to point nine centimorgan. T L R four carried a missense change in one strain, a null mutation in another. The method was needed because the gene was known only from its effect.
scenes.visual: Chromosome 4 then gene with repeat; mouse interval narrowing to Tlr4 with two strain mutations; source tags.
scenes.caption: In 1983, Gusella and colleagues linked the Huntington disease gene to a marker on chromosome 4. In 1993 the collaborative group found an unstable, expanded CAG repeat in a new gene there, in all 75 families tested. A decade separated map from gene. In 1998, Beutler's group used 2,093 meioses to confine the mouse mutation behind LPS resistance to 0.9 centimorgan. Tlr4 carried a missense change in one strain, a null mutation in another. The method was needed because the gene was known only from its effect.

scenes.tts: In 2006, Cox, Woods and colleagues mapped inability to feel pain, in three consanguineous Pakistani families, to chromosome two. They found three different homozygous truncating mutations in S C N nine A. Mutant channels expressed in H E K two ninety-three cells gave currents no greater than background. Keep this rule: linkage finds a region; different mutations in unrelated families show which gene.
